response.sql: WITH examination_sex AS (SELECT CASE WHEN p.SEX IS NULL THEN 'missing' WHEN TRIM(p.SEX) = '' THEN 'blank' ELSE 'recorded' END AS sex_group, CASE WHEN p.SEX IS NULL THEN NULL WHEN TRIM(p.SEX) = '' THEN '' ELSE p.SEX END AS sex FROM Examination e JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = e.ID), by_sex AS (SELECT sex_group, sex, COUNT(*) AS examined_count FROM examination_sex GROUP BY sex_group, sex), totals AS (SELECT SUM(examined_count) AS overall_total, AVG(CAST(examined_count AS REAL)) AS per_sex_average FROM by_sex) SELECT 'sex' AS row_type, b.sex_group, b.sex, b.examined_count, 1.0 * b.examined_count / t.overall_total AS share_of_total, NULL AS average_share, NULL AS average_above_per_sex_average FROM by_sex b CROSS JOIN totals t UNION ALL SELECT 'above_average', NULL, NULL, COALESCE(SUM(b.examined_count), 0), NULL, AVG(1.0 * b.examined_count / t.overall_total), AVG(b.examined_count - t.per_sex_average) FROM by_sex b CROSS JOIN totals t WHERE b.examined_count > t.per_sex_average

assumptions.assumption: Each examination row counts as one examination. The per-sex average is the mean count across sex groups with examinations. Empty and whitespace-only sex values form the blank group; NULL forms the missing group.

alternatives.interpretation: Count distinct patients who had an examination, rather than examination rows.
